content.comment_body: Hello, I am experiencing issues connecting to the new [product_name] running [version_no] via both my private home network and the internet. Previously, with [version_no], everything worked properly. To enable web server access, I selected the option to allow HTTP access, assigned a password, and configured the device with IP 192.168.1.50, the computer with IP 192.168.1.20, and the router at 192.168.1.1. The device responds to ping from my PC, but when I try to access it from a browser on the intranet, the connection is refused. I have attached screenshots in case there is an error.
Can you clarify what you mean by internet? Are you referring to your private home network or the broader web?
I am unable to connect from both the private home network and the web.
I noticed you changed the topic title. Previously, the word "Intranet" was not included.

That's correct, I edited the post because I hadn't explained the issue clearly. My main problem is not being able to connect to the device via intranet inside my home network. Access over the internet doesn't work either, but I think it's best to resolve the intranet connection first.
In my first post, I asked this question, and you answered differently. Now your response is confusing me.
I've updated the original post to clarify my question. Apologies for any confusion.
Please enter the URL as shown in the attachment. Additionally, install the CA certificate.
English is preferred in this forum. Please write your future posts in English. Thank you.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is unable to access the web server on [product_name] with [version_no] via both their local network and the internet, although the earlier [version_no] posed no such issues. Network configuration and IP addresses seem functional, and a ping test succeeds, but browser access remains blocked. This points toward possible changes or technical limitations with network or web server functionality between versions, leading to uncertainty and user frustration.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects seamless and reliable web server access to the newer [product_name] using the same network configuration that worked with the older version.
